MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Which of these is a chemist?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele is a chemist. Carl Wilhelm Scheele (German: [ˈʃeːlə], Swedish: [ˈɧêːlɛ]; 9 December 1742 – 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.
What is the atomic number of Oganesson?
Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Pythagoras born?
Pythagoras: Pythagoras of Samos (Ancient Greek: Πυθαγόρας; c. 570 – c. 495 BC) was an ancient Ionian Greek philosopher, polymath, and the eponymous founder of Pythagoreanism.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Dassault Rafale based?
Dassault Rafale: France. Dassault built a technology demonstrator that first flew in July 1986 as part of an eight-year flight-test programme, paving the way for approval of the project.
Who is credited with discovering Horologium?

Horologium (constellation): Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.
Who is credited with discovering Hubble's law?
Hubble's law: Georges Lemaître. The Friedmann equations showed the universe might be expanding, and presented the expansion speed if that were the case.
Who is credited with discovering Eris?
Eris (dwarf planet): Michael E. Brown. Eris (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
Hiding in coffee, fresh bread, and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is also what your liver makes when breaking down alcohol — and a prime culprit behind the morning-after hangover. What is it?
Acetaldehyde (IUPAC systematic name ethanal) is an organic chemical compound with the formula CH3CH=O.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.
Whether contracted through the skin, the lungs, or the gut, this Bacillus-driven infection can take up to two months to show symptoms — what is it?
Anthrax is an infection caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis or Bacillus cereus biovar anthracis.
This common vision condition occurs when the cornea or lens is slightly egg-shaped rather than spherical, causing blurred vision at any distance. What is it?
Astigmatism is a type of refractive error due to rotational asymmetry in the eye's refractive power.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
First described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado, this sauropod dinosaur's Greek name means arm lizard, a reference to its proportionately long front limbs — what genus is it?
Brachiosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
This group of diseases involves uncontrolled cell growth, includes over 100 types, and is responsible for about 33% of deaths when linked to tobacco and alcohol. What disease are we discussing?
Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.
Also known by the taxonomic synonym Epilobium, this hardy perennial in the willowherb family is native throughout the temperate north — which plant?
Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.
This neurological disorder strikes one side of the head around the eye and temple, often at the very same hour each day for an 8-to-10-week stretch before vanishing for months — what condition is it?
Cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by episodes of severe headaches on one side of the head, typically around the eye and temple, lasting between 15 minutes to three hours.
Native to Europe and Western Asia, this birch-family shrub produces the round nuts sold commercially as hazelnuts — which species?
Corylus avellana is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae.

This common cough suppressant found in cold medicine was combined with bupropion in 2022 to create a fast-acting antidepressant, despite belonging to the same chemical class as morphine — what drug is it?
Dextromethorphan is a cough suppressant used in many cough and cold medicines.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
In this rapid-onset condition the immune system attacks the peripheral nerves, so weakness creeps up from the feet and hands — and about 15% of patients need a ventilator. What is it?
Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.

The reciprocal cross to the more common mule, this equine hybrid is the offspring of a male horse and a female donkey, differing from its counterpart in both physiology and temperament — what is it called?
Hinny is a domestic equine hybrid, the offspring of a male horse (a stallion) and a female donkey (a jenny).

This phenomenon describes how a system's state depends on its history, as when a magnet holds different moments depending on past field changes — it underlies memory in a hard disk drive. What is it called?
Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.
Linked to a herpesvirus and immune suppression, this cancer causing purple skin lesions was already being described by Hippocrates in the 300s BC — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is a type of cancer that can form masses on the skin, in lymph nodes, in the mouth, or in other organs.
Representing the Nemean Lion slain by Heracles as one of his twelve labors, this zodiac constellation sits between Cancer and Virgo — which constellation?
Leo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac, between Cancer, the Crab, to the west and Virgo, the Maiden, to the east.
Credited as the 'Father of Cinematography' for filming Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888, this French inventor mysteriously vanished in 1890 before cinema took off — who was he?

Louis Le Prince (28 August 1841 - disappeared 16 September 1890; declared dead 16 September 1897) was a French artist and the inventor of an early motion-picture camera, and director of Roundhay Garden Scene.
This Italian economist served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022 after previously heading the European Central Bank for eight years and the Bank of Italy before that — who is he?

Mario Draghi (born 3 September 1947) is an Italian politician, economist, academic, banker, statesman, and civil servant, who served as the prime minister of Italy from 13 February 2021 to 22 October 2022.
This medical condition is diagnosed when the erect length of the affected organ measures at least two and a half standard deviations below the average size for age — what condition is it?
Micropenis is an unusually small penis.
With shells that are elongated and wedge-shaped rather than round, these bivalves attach themselves to shorelines using threads nicknamed a "beard" — what are they?
Mussel is the common name used for members of several families of bivalve molluscs, from saltwater and freshwater habitats.
Catalyzed in nature by iron-bearing nitrogenase enzymes and famously partnered with legumes, this process turns molecular N2 into ammonia — what's it called?
Nitrogen fixation is a chemical process by which molecular dinitrogen (N2) is converted into ammonia (NH3).
All 14 species of this slim-bodied, dense-furred mammal are semiaquatic, and they're famous for playful antics like sliding into the water and juggling stones — what is it?
Otter are carnivorous mammals in the subfamily Lutrinae.
It comes in a G version for the needle and a V version for the mouth, and it owes its name to the very mould it's coaxed from — which medication?
Penicillin (PCN or PEN) are a group of beta-lactam antibiotics originally obtained from Penicillium moulds, principally P. chrysogenum.
This scientific term for a group of fin-footed, mostly marine mammals includes walruses, sea lions, fur seals, and true earless seals — 34 living species in all. What is the term?
Pinniped are a widely distributed and diverse clade of carnivorous, fin-footed, semiaquatic, mostly marine mammals.
Bloating, mood swings, breast tenderness and irritability that flare in the week or two before menstruation and fade once bleeding begins — what disruptive condition is this?
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a disruptive set of emotional and physical symptoms that regularly occur in the one to two weeks before the start of each menstrual period.

Named for the ragged appearance of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants native mainly to North America has become an invasive nuisance in parts of Europe due to climate change — what plant is it?
Ragweed are flowering plants in the genus Ambrosia in the aster family, Asteraceae.

This long-term skin condition causes facial redness, pimples, and swelling, and can lead to a severely enlarged, reddened nose in extreme cases — its exact cause remains unknown — name this condition?
Rosacea is a long-term skin condition that typically affects the face.
About 950 species of these spiny, globe-shaped marine animals crawl the seabed on tube feet, found from tide pools down to 5,000 metres deep. What are they?
Sea urchin are the class Echinoidea within the echinoderms.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
A small Eurasian mustelid that turns brilliant white in winter, this animal's coat — known as ermine — once draped Catholic monarchs and the Infant Jesus of Prague — what is it?
Stoat (Mustela erminea), also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.
Named for a U.S. state where its discovery research was based, this synthetic element (symbol Ts) holds the second-highest atomic number of all and was the most recently discovered — what is it?
Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.

This parasite can infect nearly any warm-blooded animal, but can only sexually reproduce inside cats, and is famous for altering infected rodents' behavior to make them less afraid of feline predators — what parasite is it?
Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic alveolate that causes toxoplasmosis.
Just 25 light-years away, this is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra and the fifth-brightest star in the entire night sky — what is it?
Vega is the brightest star in the northern constellation of Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.
Brought to Asia by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this tropical American tree produces a knobby, sweet fruit known as sugar apple or custard apple — what is this plant?
Annona squamosa: Species of tree. Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
Its guanidino group serves as the biological precursor for nitric oxide production, and this amino acid earned the one-letter code 'R' purely for phonetic reasons — what is it?
Arginine: Amino acid. Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.

Nicknamed 'Huey,' this American utility helicopter became the first turbine-powered rotorcraft in U.S. military service, developed in the 1950s to meet an Army need for medical evacuation and utility missions. Which aircraft?
Bell UH-1 Iroquois: Huey family of American military utility helicopters.
This medical term for blood escaping the circulatory system describes a healthy person as able to lose 10 to 15 percent of their total volume without serious harm — what is it called?
Bleeding: Blood escaping from the circulatory system. Bleeding, hemorrhage, haemorrhage or blood loss, is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.
Making up just 2.6 percent of the brain's weight, this stalk-like structure connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and houses all ten pairs of cranial nerve origins — what is it?
Brainstem: Posterior part of the brain, adjoining and structurally continuous.
Its Latin name means "chisel-bearing," a nod to the stout egg-laying organs of its members — which insect suborder includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera: Suborder of insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
A founder of humanistic psychology, this American psychologist pioneered person-centered therapy, an approach that also shaped student-centered learning in education — who is he?
Certified in 1984 and developed into a freighter variant for FedEx, this single-engine turboprop utility plane typically seats nine and can be fitted with floats or skis — which aircraft?
Cessna 208 Caravan: Family of utility transport aircraft.

Most often documented in boxers and football players, this neurodegenerative disease is linked to repeated blows to the head and can worsen into dementia — what's its name, usually shortened to three letters?
Chronic traumatic encephalopathy: Neurodegenerative disease caused by head injury.
Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this plant genus produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and brewed into one of the world's most valuable traded commodities — which genus?
Found only in placental mammals, this roughly four-inch bundle of 200 to 300 million nerve fibers is the brain's largest white-matter structure, linking its left and right hemispheres — what is it?
Corpus callosum: White matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.

Sometimes nicknamed a 'cat' though it's actually the sole living member of its own genus in the weasel family, this North American forest mammal has been trapped for its fur since the 1700s — what is it?
Fisher (animal): Species of small, carnivorous mammal native to North America.

Unlike plants, this kingdom of life can't photosynthesize, and unlike most things, it has chitin in its cell walls — feeding instead by oozing digestive enzymes out and absorbing what dissolves. What group includes yeasts, molds, and mushrooms?
Fungus: Organism belonging to kingdom Fungi.
Endemic to China and sporting a handy 'thumb' on its forepaw to grip bamboo, this black-and-white bear weighs in around 100 to 115 kg — what animal is it?
Giant panda: Species of bear. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China.
This large, widely distributed white wading bird nests in colonies built in trees near water and is now expanding its range into northern Europe — which species?
Great egret: Species of bird. The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.
This German-American physicist won a 1967 Nobel Prize for explaining how a nuclear cycle powers heavy stars, after heading the Theoretical Division at Los Alamos during World War II — who is he?
Also nicknamed 'rose mallow,' this genus of large, showy tropical flowers includes both herbaceous plants and woody shrubs — which genus is it?
Hibiscus: Genus of plants. Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
In its pure form it's a faintly blue, syrupy liquid, but the concentrated 'high-test' version decomposes explosively when heated and has even been used as rocket fuel — what compound is it?
Hydrogen peroxide: Chemical compound. The molecule hydrogen peroxide is asymmetrical and highly polarized.

Named for the indigo-blue line seen in its spectrum when discovered in 1863, this soft, silvery-white metal with atomic number 49 is used to make the transparent conductive coating on flat-panel displays — what is it?
Indium: Chemical element with atomic number 49 (In)
An English mathematician who shaped matrix and invariant theory, he founded the American Journal of Mathematics while leading the field at Johns Hopkins — who was he?
This British-American designer ran industrial design at Apple alongside Steve Jobs, then founded the creative collective LoveFrom working with Ferrari and OpenAI — who is he?
The largest joint in the human body, it's a modified hinge that links the thigh to the lower leg via two separate joints — what is it?
Knee: Leg joint in primates. The knee is a modified hinge joint, which permits flexion and extension as well as slight internal and external rotation.

This small wild feline of South and Southeast Asia sports dark spots on a tawny coat and two stripes running from its eyes to its ears, and can live as high as 4,474 meters in the Himalayas — what is it?
Leopard cat: Small wild cat species. The leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis) is a small wild cat with dark spots on the tawny-coloured body and limbs.
This American WWII twin-engine, twin-boom fighter carried its pilot alone in a central nacelle and served as fighter-bomber, night fighter, and long-range escort — which aircraft was it?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning: American twin-engined fighter of WWII. The Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
This biological term covers the pairing of organisms for sexual reproduction, encompassing everything from copulation to external fertilization in fish and amphibians — what is it?
Mating: Process of pairing in biology.
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two mirror-image enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride-salt form nicknamed 'crystal' — what is it?
This synthetic prostaglandin medication treats stomach ulcers, induces labor, and — often paired with mifepristone — is used to end a pregnancy. What drug is it?
Misoprostol: Medication to induce abortion and treat ulcers.
Native to the Americas from Texas down to Argentina, this domesticated waterfowl species has also gone feral in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe — which species?
Muscovy duck: Species of bird. The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.
Named after a German physical chemist, this electrochemistry formula calculates a reaction's reduction potential from temperature, electron count, and reactant concentrations — which relationship?
Nernst equation: Physical law in electrochemistry.
Practitioners of this field are sometimes mistaken for mere coin collectors, but they study all means of paying debts — even the horses the Kyrgyz once used as currency. What's the field called?
Numismatics: Study of currencies, coins and paper money.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?

This informal name applies to any shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc — a body plan that evolved independently many times through convergent evolution across unrelated lineages. What creature is it?
Slug: Shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc. Slug or land slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.

Numbering more than 9,000 species, these tiny hexapods are no longer classified as true insects and get their scientific class name from Greek words meaning 'glue' and 'peg,' after a structure called the collophore — what are they called?
Known in antiquity as 'oil of vitriol,' this odorless, syrupy liquid is so thirsty for water that it never occurs pure in nature and will char nearly anything it touches — which substance is it?

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.

What is the chemical symbol for krypton?
The symbol for krypton is Kr. Krypton is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.
